key_insight: Direct stochastic optimization of battery dispatch can cut equivalent carbon emissions in PV-battery homes far more effectively than heuristic self-consumption control, approaching the best-case benchmark.
engineering_relevance: The study shows that tractable linear stochastic programming can guide emission-aware battery scheduling in residential solar storage systems under uncertain load, generation, and grid carbon intensity.
method: Compared a hierarchy of linear battery models from rule-based self-consumption to stochastic programs with linear feedback.
Generated large scenario sets using principal component analysis of real operational data.
Evaluated models against an omniscient benchmark and unseen synthetic-realistic scenarios.
evidence_signal: On synthetic yet realistic scenarios, the programmed battery model achieved emission reductions close to the omniscient lower bound, while feedback models did not generalize better on test data.
watch_item: The scenario-based formulation can be computationally expensive and its performance depends on how well the training scenarios capture future uncertainty.
paper_title: Comparative Analysis of Linear Battery Models for Carbon Emission Optimization in Solar Energy Systems
